### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/object.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via ObjectSchemaBase (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via imageField (symbol, a field of const object ObjectSchemaBase, an authorable key of data/Object), imageField (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in refuseNonPictureImageField))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/object.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ce4e205e2b6abd7a49f98a27cd8297a1e52f828b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d4099f859ca4ec1d1e3646ee333906d868b0a17a` — the merge of head `06cb584a8a9c279870b50dfa7a8b2ba56e1fa3a6` into base `ce4e205e2b6abd7a49f98a27cd8297a1e52f828b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d4099f859ca4ec1d1e3646ee333906d868b0a17a && git checkout d4099f859ca4ec1d1e3646ee333906d868b0a17a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ce4e205e2b6abd7a49f98a27cd8297a1e52f828b 06cb584a8a9c279870b50dfa7a8b2ba56e1fa3a6 && git checkout -B drift-repro ce4e205e2b6abd7a49f98a27cd8297a1e52f828b && git merge --no-ff 06cb584a8a9c279870b50dfa7a8b2ba56e1fa3a6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ce4e205e2b6abd7a49f98a27cd8297a1e52f828b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ce4e205e2b6abd7a49f98a27cd8297a1e52f828b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `06cb584a8a9c279870b50dfa7a8b2ba56e1fa3a6`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #21182 (body and both comments, the claim and the `os-dev-report`), PR #21221 (body, 12-file list, net diff `origin/main...06cb584a`, merge base `862f12c0`), the check-runs on the head, `origin/main` and the pinned objectui checkout at `.objectui-sha` `31971ff1` as read-only references. Nothing was built, run or re-run; every gate verdict below is the head's own check-run conclusion.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against `origin/main`:

1. **`ObjectSchema` widens by one optional key, `imageField: string`.** Before: the strict shape refused the key as `unrecognized_keys`. After: accepted when it names an own key of `fields` whose parsed `type` is `image` or `avatar`; otherwise ONE `custom` issue at `['imageField']`. Nothing that parsed before is refused, so the net movement is a pure widening. **Right**, and it is what card scope 1 and 2 ask for.
2. **The refusal rides `ObjectSchema`'s existing `superRefine`**, beside `refuseForeignTreeReference`. `fields` is a `z.record` (not an array), so own-property lookup is the correct resolution and the prototype-name case is refused rather than resolved (pinned). The judgment reaches all three authoring doors through the one schema: `ObjectSchema.create()` / `defineStack`, `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` (`os validate`, issue at `['objects', 0, 'imageField']`), and `getMetadataTypeSchema('object')` (the metadata save door). Each door is pinned in `object-image-field.test.ts`. **Right.** I confirmed the dev's premise myself: no door on `origin/main` refuses `nameField` for an undeclared name (`display-name.ts#objectTitleCompleteness` returns `synthesized`, `validate-object-field-refs.ts` leaves the scalar pointers out by its own header), so there was no `nameField` door to reuse.
3. **Prescription text.** Names both accepted types and both factories (`Field.image()` / `Field.avatar()`), no tracker number in any runtime string; `IMAGE_FIELD_TYPES` is the single list read by the check and spelled into the message. `IMAGE_FIELD_TYPES` and `refuseNonPictureImageField` are module-private, so no new export. **Right.**
4. **`ObjectExtensionSchema` is unchanged**: strict, no `imageField`, so the pointer is only ever the owning object's. **Right**, and no new refusal is owed there since an extension cannot carry the key.
5. **Published-surface prose.** The `.describe()`, the TSDoc, the changeset and the `objects.mdx` row all say no renderer draws the key yet and that an empty field draws nothing (no initials or placeholder). That is the ruling's wording and keeps the claim as narrow as the enforcement (Prime Directive #10). **Right.**
6. **Generated and ratcheted artefacts**, each checked for whether it should have moved: `authorable-surface/data.json` (+`data/Object:imageField`) moved; `authorable-surface.base.json` is the frozen anchor at `baseRev` and correctly did not; `json-schema.manifest/**` is a ratchet of def names, not properties, and correctly did not; `packages/spec/json-schema/` is gitignored; `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` is keyed per schema and `data/Object` already carries its `superRefine` row, so no new row is owed; `api-surface` is symbol-level and no symbol was exported; `content/docs/references/**` (3 pages, 4 tables) regenerated; `liveness/object.json` +1 `planned` row and `state-counts/object.md` 51 → 52. The metadata-protocol `/meta/types` pin for `object` moves 43 → 44 on the `field` 74 → 75 precedent written in that same comment. The `reference-sites` derivation rejects `*Field` spellings by rule, so `imageField` is correctly not a reference site. **All right.**
7. **Liveness row** `object.imageField` = `planned`, `evidenceScope: cross-repo`, `verifiedAt` 2026-10-01, evidence anchored to `object.zod.ts#refuseNonPictureImageField` (gate-checkable symbol) plus the objectui realm pointer at the pin. I re-read objectui at `31971ff1`: `containers.tsx` has 0 `imageField` hits and 4 `nameField` hits; the only `imageField` hits in the repo are the gallery view's legacy option. Not `authorWarn`'d, on liveness README rule 1 (display metadata must NOT be marked) and the `app.branding.logo` row, whose wording this row follows. `Spec property liveness` is green on the head. **Right.**
8. **Form ↔ Zod reconciliation**: one `omit` row for `object.(root).imageField` in the declared-not-enforced group, worded after `externalSharingModel`. Studio does not offer the key until it is enforced. **Right**; whether to offer it is left for the enforcement, as the row says.
9. **JSON Schema expressivity (note, not a defect of this diff).** The "names an `image`/`avatar` field" rule is a `custom` check and cannot project into the published JSON Schema, the same class as the tree-reference rule; a validator reading the published file alone accepts a bad pointer. This is the existing `data/Object` dropped-refinement row, not a new one.

Public-surface changes beyond the schema: the exported types `ServiceObject` / `ServiceObjectParsed` gain one optional property (additive); no runtime package other than `@objectstack/spec` changes code (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` moves a test pin only).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/21182-object-image-field.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **`minor`**, body line `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; PR body `Clause-②: yes`. A new optional key with a refusal that only fires when the new key is set is a widening of the accept set; `yes` takes at least `minor`, and `minor` is what is declared. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` publishes nothing from this diff (test only), so no second changeset is owed. The changeset's claim that the save door answers `422 INVALID_METADATA` matches the envelope `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` documents. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. **Clause-②: yes (widening) — matches the diff.**

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. Dev flags from the `os-dev-report` `deviations`, each answered:

1. *Door choice (Zone 2 #2 falsified in part).* **Accepted** — measured as in ①.2; the ruling asks for refusal at authoring/publish and the one `superRefine` reaches all three doors.
2. *Two files outside the claimed surface* (`metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`, `protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts`). **Accepted** — both are pins the declared key moves, both in the fixture-triage class the claim allows, neither widens scope.
3. *Planned row without `authorWarn`.* **Accepted** — README rule 1 and the `app.branding.logo` precedent, see ①.7.
4. *objectui read at the pin `31971ff1`, not the card's `8001068b9c`.* **Accepted** — the pin is the reference this repo is held to, and I re-measured the same finding there.
5. *Attribution: model-free trailer pair instead of the harness-suggested trailer.* **Accepted** — AGENTS.md's Multi-agent discipline requires exactly that pair; all four branch commits carry it, and the trailer-less merge commit is the shape `check-commit-card-trailers.mjs` exempts by name.
6. *Plain `git merge` of `origin/main` `862f12c0`, no `os-regen-merge.sh`.* **Accepted** — I diffed the merge base `e18fea6d` to `862f12c0`: main brought `packages/lint/**` and two `.changeset/*.md`, none of which `.gitattributes` routes `merge=os-regen`, and none of the branch's generated files were touched on main.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each answered:

- *`nameField` existence is refused at no door.* **Accepted as a note.** The deferral is already written into `validate-object-field-refs.ts`'s own header as a separate decision; not a defect of this diff and not this card's scope.
- *An `ObjectExtension` can override the type of the field `imageField` names.* **Accurate, and escalated to the dispatching seat.** `registry.ts#mergeObjectDefinitions` folds `fields` as `{ ...base.fields, ...extension.fields }` and the folded object is not re-parsed through the object door, so a second package can redefine the named field as a non-picture after the refusal has passed. The gap is generic to every object-level field pointer (`nameField`, `stageField`, `highlightFields`, index columns) and pre-dates this diff; no renderer reads `imageField` today, so there is no reach. Not a reason to fail this PR. Whether to file a card against the fold (re-judging the merged object through the object door) is the seat's call under Prime Directive #10; I am read-only on the tracker.
- *Studio does not offer `imageField` until enforced.* **Accepted** — the omit row records it; the offer is a ruling for when objectui#11383 lands.

Note for the dispatching seat, prose face, not a contract face: `content/docs/data-modeling/schema-design.mdx` keeps a second object-property table (`nameField`, `titleFormat`, `highlightFields`) that gained no `imageField` row. The card asked for one sentence in the object docs and `objects.mdx` carries it, so this is not a gap in the delivery.

**Check-runs on the head** (read 2026-10-01T18:32Z, after waiting for the last to conclude): 35 check-runs, 33 `success`, 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, which runs only on a `.objectui-sha` change, and the opt-in `Packed-tarball smoke`), 0 failed, 0 still running. Green on the head include `Lint & Repo Gates` (the generated-artefact, liveness, changeset, ADR-0087 and docs gate family), `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core (1–6/6)`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, all four `Type Check` jobs, `Temporal Conformance`, the three `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI`. The diff touches no governed surface.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-21182-object-image-field`
Reviewed-by: `session_01UtnxvdiN376GF3sgXwAw4d`

**VERDICT: PASS**
